blocks.text: Massive flooding in several towns and cities in Central Luzon and Metro Manila has subsided. Many are asking why it happened and whether it will happen again. Flooding arises from a complex interplay of geomorphic, climatic and human-induced factors. But recent evidence indicates that the worsening flood crisis is not simply a product of climate change. It is increasingly driven by land subsidence. While global sea levels are rising by an average of 1 to 3 millimeters annually because of climate change, parts of Central Luzon are subsiding at rates exceeding 100 millimeters per year.
